previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for a 5-day history of nonbloody diarrhea, nausea, and weakness. She presented with hypotension and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. A CT scan showed findings consistent with enteritis, suggesting an infectious cause. She was treated with IV fluids, antibiotics (ciprofloxacin and metronidazole), and supportive care. Her diet was advanced to BRAT, renal function improved, and blood pressure stabilized. Glyburide was held initially and restarted upon oral tolerance. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, follow up with her gastroenterologist, and monitor blood pressure.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
